update flying shortly after mastectomy surgery tips i originally posted on here asking for advice after my nerve preserving prophylactic mastectomy with dti and flying home a few days later i thought i would share my experience in case there is anyone out there searching like i was i had surgery on monday and flew home on friday night i was definitely ready to fly i had done smaller trips doctors office and grocery store as a test run as long as i went slow i had no issues also a really important factor was my amazing boyfriend throughout this entire process without his mental and physical support none of this wouldve been possible airport i highly recommend booking the first class ticket the extra space ease of boarding free luggage etc was all 100 worth it checking the suitcase just meant my boyfriend carried one bag for us i bought a mastectomy pillow though i only used it for car rides i found it heavy and cumbersome to use so soon after surgery however it was nice to store my passport in while going through tsa my doctor gave me a letter for tsa but because i have precheck it wasnt even needed tsa was a breeze my credit card gave us lounge access which helped us get a space to eat comfortably and settle before the flight i will say it was helpful to empty the drains before the flight my boyfriend has been doing that task for me and the family bathrooms werent the cleanest so we just elected to wait until we were home since it wasnt urgent it was a rather long travel day all considering we left our airbnb at 3pm pst and got home 7am est the next day we had one layover so it definitely was doable car rides werent bad as long as i took an ibuprofen the pain was manageablenon existent the drain sites hurt the worst my muscles from my body compensating and protecting are sore so an occasionally shoulder massage from my boyfrined helped i held off on taking the ativan because i was sleeping fine without it but i started to take it to help with muscle relaxation like my traps and it was really helpful honestly the mental battle to get to surgery day was the hardest part of this process so far the morning of the procedure i had peace with my decision and my amazing team of surgeons anesthesiologists and nurses were incredible at keeping the mood light and positive as of now 6 days post op i dont have any regrets thank you to everyone who initially commented and gave me all the wonderful tips one of the best tips was a straw i cant believe how much a silly straw made my life so much easier if there is anyone out there reading this one day and is looking for someone to talk to about traveling for surgery nerve preservation etc i would be more than happy to share more details

best use of scarce resources however i dont know if youve ever tried to run a business in a poor country it turns out that the decentralized economic systems they have are also not economically rational systematically failing to provide functioning market mechanisms that support longterm investments such as highway systems reliable electric grids municipal water treatment etc even when those things would be highly efficient uses of scarce resources rather generally speaking they systematically squander their resources in order to stabilize the existing socioeconomic power structures generally speaking if you invest your money in a historically kleptocratic country you can expect your investment to get confiscated if its profitable and possibly even if its not which is what happened to my retirement savings even if you make your investment at a time when the country is governed by nonkleptocrats you will probably lose it after the next coup or election in which new kleptocrats come to power in that environment where private investment in longterm infrastructure projects is irrational and languishing in poverty for many generations is the normal state of affairs state capitalism frequently works i dont think moral arguments about atrocities are somehow orthogonal here power plants and electrical grids are often worthwhile investments not because building monuments to westinghouse is a pious sacrifice that pleases the electrical gods but because they promote human welfare by providing material abundance thats how we measure whether society is richer not as you say by the amount of concrete poured if human welfare is your yardstick the possibility of economic catastrophes like the holodomor greatly diminishing human welfare must necessarily weigh on the negative side of the balance the inhabitants of auschwitz and the congo free state were not enjoying even the material abundance they had enjoyed previously so we know that central planning carries risks to human welfare that decentralized systems do not however it also has opportunities to promote human welfare that decentralized systems do not the variance is larger i dont think we know enough to measure the expectation bofadeez sure running a business in kleptocratic hellholes is a nightmare confiscation risks kill private investment especially for big infrastructure that needs stable property rights and enforceable contracts to make sense but thats not a bug of decentralized markets its the poison of political interference and weak institutions which state capitalism only doubles down on by swapping entrepreneurial discovery for bureaucratic fiat still without solving the calculation problem or providing systematic feedback beyond stuff got built look at hong kong in your list it boomed precisely because of its handsoff freemarket approach with toptier economic freedom rankings unlike more interventionist tigers that rode creditfueled waves but crashed in 97 or stagnated like japan postbubble atrocities are the dark side of concentrated power touted as enabling opportunities jacking up variance with no way to gauge if human welfare gains beat the unseen costs of foregone innovations without prices and profits guiding resources were left guessing expectations but history shows freer systems deliver sustainable abundance when institutions let them not coerced escapes that often loop back to poverty or worse kragen this is the right way to think about the problem if youre faced with the problem of what country to start an electric power company in but its not very helpful if youre faced with the problem of how to govern pakistan which is certainly not a hellhole but does suffer major corruption problems the political interference weak institutions concentrated power and official corruption are largely givens you can work to change them incrementally but you cant just import the government of hong kong even if you could you couldnt convince investors that the reforms would stick this time for real perhaps if you could obtain political power that you could retain stably for decades you could make pretty big changes there but only at the cost of further concentrating power creating opportunities for even greater corruption profits for whoever can wrest power away from you nobody has ever held power for decades in pakistans history even nawaz sharif didnt make it to 10 years in power over his three nonconsecutive terms if you simply liberalize economically without eliminating the confiscation risks that kill private investment private investment will not magically materialize without the private investors who are sensibly investing their savings in a 711 franchise in cleveland ohio so what can you hypothetically governing the country do under these constraints a proven strategy is public investment like airbus like the military contracts that sustain boeing like the hoover dam like the rural electrification administration like federally guaranteed student loans like the interstate highway system like volkswagen like tupolev like rosatom like industrias aeronuticas y mecnicas del estado like the apollo program like huawei like westinghouses nuclear power division like the arpanet and nsfnet certainly the money wont be invested as wisely as if savvy entrepreneurs like warren buffett were directing it and neither warren buffett nor juan pern is going to do a good job at investing in unforeseen innovations but even if most of that investment is wasted like project huemul it can still dramatically augment the economic productivity of the country under circumstances when private investment is unavailable often such productive capacity will eventually make the country more appealing to private investors but that can take a long time in this situation you arent faced with the choice between state capitalism and regular capitalism youre faced with the choice between state capitalism and no capitalism thus stateguaranteed loans to build power stations based on the dialogue and the political reality of nepal the answer is yes the situation described in the text applies almost perfectly to nepal though political scientists often use the specific term crony capitalism rather than kleptocracy to describe the nepali context here is how the arguments from kragen and bofadeez map directly to the situation in nepal 1 is nepal a kleptocracy while nepal does not have a single dictator looting the treasury like mobutu in zaire it fits the definition of a distributed kleptocracy or crony capitalism the extraction mechanism in nepal the state is often treated as a resource to be harvested by a network of politicians bureaucrats and affiliated businessmen the contractorstate a significant percentage of nepals elected officials especially at the local and provincial levels are themselves construction contractors they use their political power to award contracts to their own firms fitting kragens description of squandering resources to stabilize existing socioeconomic power structures systemic corruption transparency international consistently ranks nepal poorly the melamchi water supply project is the ultimate example of this see below 2 how the text applies to us nepal the debate between kragen and bofadeez explains exactly why nepal is stuck in its current economic trap kragens point private investment is irrational kragen argues that in a corrupt country it makes no sense to invest private money because the government might steal it or demand bribes that destroy profitability nepal reality this is exactly what happened with the melamchi water supply project the italian contractor cmc di ravenna abandoned the project in 20182019 why they alleged that highranking nepali bureaucrats demanded a 3 cut commission on payments that were legally owed to them result the confiscation risk kragen mentions became real the foreign investor realized they couldnt operate fairly so they left this validates kragens point why would a foreign company build a highway or grid in nepal if the government will just extort them once the concrete is poured kragens point squandering resources to stabilize power kragen argues that poor countries dont fail by accident they fail because the money is used to keep elites in power rather than build things nepal reality nepal has had over a dozen different governments in the last 15 years the budget is often sliced up to satisfy coalition partners distributive politics rather than following a rational national master plan the porkbarrel spending funds given to mps to spend in their own districts with little oversight is a direct example of using resources to stabilize political power rather than build efficient infrastructure bofadeezs point the poison of political interference bofadeez argues that state involvement fails because of weak institutions and lack of market feedback nepal reality this explains why nepals stateled projects like the national airline nepal airlines or the various governmentrun sugarcement factories of the past often go bankrupt or stagnate the directors are appointed based on political loyalty the power structure rather than competence counterexample state capitalism success interestingly nepal does have one example that supports kragens defense of state capitalism kulman ghising and the nepal electricity authority nea the nea is a state monopoly for years it was corrupt and nepal had 18 hours of loadshedding blackouts when a competent leader ghising was given authority he fixed the grid using state powersomething the fragmented private sector hadnt managed to do this proves kragens point that sometimes state capitalism is the only way to get a grid built in a poor country provided the kleptocrats step aside for a moment summary the user is correct the text is effectively describing nepal 1 investment is dangerous because bureaucrats demand cuts melamchi 2 infrastructure lags not because of a lack of money but because the money is used for political patronage 3 the choice nepal is currently trapped in the scenario kragen describeswhere world powers weavers term saw the protectorate involved in the 1978 cambodianvietnamese war on the side of the socialist republic of vietnam to overthrow the khmer rouge regime in cambodia as well as becoming involved in the soviet counterinsurgency campaign in afghanistan beginning in 1982 and taking an active role in providing technical assistance in response to the chernobyl disaster while weaver was american and generally more conservative than frolov or his successor relations between the protectorate and the western bloc soured significantly during the latter years of his term weaver passed away in 1988 being succeeded by his east german chief of staff and close friend of erich honecker general field marshal johann fincke fincke was immensely sympathetic to the eastern bloc and believed that the protectorate forces should become far more actively involved with world affairs while finckes dream of salvaging the eastern bloc was always a fantasy he did obtain the deployment of the protectorate navy to blockade south africa in 1991 when the protectorateled investigation into the crash of south african airways flight 295 revealed that the airline had been used by the absorbing former stasi personnel during this time the protectorate also absorbed a great deal of formerly east german industry renovating and modernising it and providing the protectorate forces with a reliable and autonomous source of material fincke died in 2005 being succeeded by general air marshal li daiyu the first female supreme commander in the history of the protectorate daiyu allegedly chosen for having saved finckes life in 1994 when protectorate one the aircraft which carries the supreme commander was crippled shortly after takeoff by a catastrophic engine failure daiyu was quite the opposite of fincke being rather timid and moderate at a time during which the protectorate desperately needed strong leadership daiyu died unexpectedly on 2 january 2021 and was succeeded by grand admiral gregorio arnesi who had not expected to take up the office for at least another decade organisation overall strategic command authority for the protectorate forces rests with the supreme commander or oberbefehlshaber who is elected for life by the protectorate forces high council which comprises representatives of all major branches daytoday operations fall to the chief of the general generalstabsrat which comprises the supreme commander chief of the general staff chief of the army staff chief of the naval staff chief of the air staff chief of the military security service and prepared to move immediately the army also includes army aviation which maintains rotary wing aircraft for transport and close air support the protectorate navy is built around its sixteen carrier
